title: Evolution and heterogeneity of lethal metastatic bladder cancer subtypes.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Paper is paywalled (no PMCID; the Nature page redirects to a login). Found the GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) SuperSeries GSE302273 by searching GEO, with matching summary and authors (Ha, Hsieh, Lam, Haffner). Downloaded GSE301508_for_geo_Met_CPM_COUNTS_allsamples.txt.gz (1.9 MB): 19,712 genes x 67 metastasis samples from 19 patient IDs, integer counts despite the 'CPM' name. Its series matrix lists 68 samples and gives only tissue site, 'Metastatic' and 'Flash-frozen' as sample fields; there is no histological subtype, survival or clinical column. GSE302781 (single-nucleus RNA sequencing): file list read, 15 samples as 10x matrix/barcodes/features, 425 MB tar file not downloaded; its sample fields carry only patient ID, with no cell-type annotation.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Cohort size (20 patients, 104 tumours, per news coverage and the abstract), whole-genome/exome sequencing, cell-free DNA, histological subtype calls and survival come from the abstract or secondary reports. I found no open DNA-sequencing deposit; human germline-level data is presumably in controlled access, but I could not confirm this because the data availability statement was not retrievable.

a1_downloadable.note: Bulk RNA and single-nucleus RNA count matrices are openly downloadable from GEO (checked). The genomic data behind the main findings (evolution trees, mutations, cell-free DNA) was not found in any open repository.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked in the GEO files: the only sample fields are tissue site, patient ID and 'Metastatic'. Histological subtype, survival and seeding pattern would have to be pulled from the paywalled paper's supplement and joined by hand.

a3_inputs_present.note: Expression counts are present with gene symbols (checked).

a4_units_stated.note: Bulk file has integer read counts; the 'CPM' (counts per million) in the file name doesn't match the integer values, which is a minor unit ambiguity (checked).

a5_enough_rows.note: 67 bulk tumour samples from 19 patients (counted); any clinical or subtype label is per patient, so n is about 20, far below 400.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Bulk file has 67 columns while the series matrix lists 68 samples (an extra 'Metastatic 18-101' renal pelvis sample), and the paper reports 104 tumours. Most tumours have DNA data only, which is not openly deposited.

a8_label_provenance.note: Subtype calls would come from pathologist review (a physical measurement), per the abstract; not verified.

honest_claim_h3: With 19 patients, a model could at best show that expression separates histological subtypes in these patients' metastases; it could not support any claim that generalises.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use tumour gene expression from autopsy metastases to predict histological subtype and patient survival in metastatic bladder cancer.
plain_idea.train_on: Gene expression of 19,712 genes for each of 67 metastases from 19 patients (verified), with patient as the unit.
plain_idea.predict: Histological subtype (pathologist-assigned) or survival. Neither is in the open files; both would be copied from the paywalled paper's supplement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Oncologists would like a non-invasive way to flag aggressive plasmacytoid or neuroendocrine disease, but 19 patients can't train or validate such a model.

ml_idea: Classify histological subtype from bulk metastasis RNA (RNA sequencing) with leave-one-patient-out evaluation. Not viable: about 20 patients, and the labels are not in the deposited files.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; rejected at Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count distinct patients in the bulk matrix column prefixes: 19 (done, kills it).

verdict_reason: Fails A5 and A2. The open GEO data is 67 metastases from 19 patients with no subtype or survival column, so any patient-level label means about 20 examples copied from a paywalled supplement. The DNA data behind the paper's main results was not found openly. The existing-models audit was skipped because Part A failed.
